title: Does Tiny Tapeout's real tile-size table change which keyword-spotting model fits a tile?
lede: Tiny Tapeout's real SKY130 tile sizes (1x1 is 161 × 111.52 µm = 17,955 µm², 0.43% below the value assumed earlier) applied to the synthesised keyword-spotting engine and the retrained models: the best 1x1 model is unchanged at 100% and 50% utilisation and flips at 70% (H = 16, 4-bit, 0.596 instead of 8-bit, 0.616, a 29 µm² miss); H = 64 with 8-bit weights (0.737) fits a 1x2 tile.
summary: accel-ttfit assumed a 161 × 112 µm tile from a search snippet. This project fetches Tiny Tapeout's own SKY130 tile table (1x1 = 17,955 µm², 0.43% smaller) and re-fits the synthesised keyword-spotting engine (6,300–24,500 µm²) with the retrained accuracies of accel-ttretrain over all 12 tile sizes at 100, 70 and 50% utilisation. One 1x1 tile: the best model is unchanged at 100% (H = 32, 8-bit, 0.693) and 50% (H = 16, 3-bit, 0.563) and flips at 70% (H = 16, 4-bit, 0.596, because the 8-bit model misses by 29 µm²). A 1x2 tile holds H = 64 with 8-bit weights (0.737), the largest model swept. Utilisation is assumed, area is synthesis-only, accuracy is on a substitute feature set; the tile table itself is sourced.
